summary: Whitby Lighthouse stood on the west pier of Whitby Harbour, Lake Ontario, about 48 km east of Toronto; its 1857 octagonal tower was removed in 1958, and two pier lights mark the entrance today.

light.note: Current East Pierhead light (CCG 504). first_lit is the first lighthouse on the west pier per the 1899 history quoted by LF.

skeletal tower, new concrete east pier

corrections.why: The 1899 history, as quoted by LighthouseFriends, says the lighthouse on the west pier was established in 1844. The 1857 date belongs to the larger octagonal tower built that year. Needs a human check of the 1899 book itself.

corrections.current: tower 6.5 m standing; tower 4.0 m standing (both present-day pier lights)
corrections.proposed: add: octagonal wooden tower, built 1857 on the west pier, removed 1958
corrections.why: The record lists only the present-day pier lights. The 1857 tower is the station's historic light and is absent.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The structure a source calls lost is the 1857 wooden lighthouse, removed in 1958. The standing structures OSM maps today are the present East Pierhead and West Breakwater lights (CCG entries 504 and 505).

LF's 1899 history gives 1844 for the first lighthouse on the west pier; LF and Rowlett date the larger octagonal tower to 1857. Both are true of different structures; the record's 1857 is the tower's date.

LF says the 1958 removal was followed by a move to the Muckle farm west of Cranberry Marsh; Rowlett says it was demolished when the piers were rebuilt in 1958. Both give 1958; they differ on its fate.

notes_for_editor: The 1899 History of the Great Lakes is read only through LighthouseFriends; no copy is in the corpus. The 1844 first lighthouse date, the harbour sales and the 1899 description all depend on that quotation, so check the book before publishing. LighthouseFriends gives no document for the 1857 designer (McDermott) or contractor (Chisholm). The 1915 fifth-order lens rests on LighthouseFriends alone. An earlier note pointed to a '6th order dioptric lens' for Whitby in the 1915-16 Marine report (scan 61, printed 54); on the page image there is no Whitby entry on scan 61 or on scan 59 (printed 52), so that pointer is withdrawn. The Toronto District pages of that report were not located, so no Marine report in the corpus confirms or contradicts the 1915 order. Keeper dates were matched by position and then checked on the page image: the 1910 keeper list (report p. 267, scan 269) prints the Whitby row as Port Whitby Hbr. Co. Ltd., May 1, 1905. The 1915 keeper table (fiscal 1914-15 report, scan 88, printed 81) has 'R. Goldring' appointed Dec. 2, 1911, but its station column could not be read reliably, so the story uses LF's 1911 date only. The 1916-17 repair row (report p. 39, scan 46) was checked on the page image: Whitby, repairs to lighthouse, day labour, M. J. Egan under 'Contractor or foreman', 206.82. The 1923-24 Aga entry (report p. 32, scan 39) is quoted from the corpus page. Marine report 'Whitby' entries in the 1914 to 1919 lists of registered ports and of buoys or beacons were not used. Ownership: no source read names the owner of the present East Pierhead or West Breakwater lights; Rowlett says the 1857 tower was built by the municipal government, while LF names the Port Whitby Harbor Company as keeper, so the owner is unresolved. Access: Rowlett describes the east pier as walkable with the tower closed; confirm current access before publication. Storms and wrecks: no event tied to this station was found in the sources read, so the story has no storms chapter. Not searched: Chronicling America (no Ontario coverage expected), the Whitby Free Press 1980 article LF cites, and the Directory of Federal Heritage Designations, so heritage status is not stated. Record: the first_lit date is corrected to 1844 for the first light (see corrections); the 1857 date is the tower's. Agency: the CCG list includes both present pier lights; the record's agency is null.
